title: Looking for feedback for my japanese retro inspired racing rougelike "Tougelike"
author: noz_
selftext:
Hey r/aigemdev \- some of you might remember the protype i posted about 2 months ago to the "[I'll rate your AI game](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1whzopm/ill_rate_your_ai_game/)" thread, that got alot of positive feedback - since then ive been working on it in my freetime and made it a proper rougelike with alot more complexity and polish - new 3d models, way more complex gameplay, more cars etc.

I would love to have some feedback and playtesters to find the missing gaps in it and improve it even further - the game is free and will remain free. just accessed via browser, works on any system, phones included. (small trick, if you are on your phone you can click the share button and then "add to home screen" you can play it fullscreen/landscape like a proper app. works on chrome desktop aswelll).

I also created a [discord](https://discord.com/invite/rX5sCHsW6j) to share more complex feedback and bugs, feel free to use but you can also keep it in this thread. Updates will instantly appear on the website and its changelog, but on the discord aswell with more details. i will add anybody that posts gameplay feedback and bugs there to the credits (unless you dont want it).

Play it here: [https://njlent.de/tougelike/](https://njlent.de/tougelike/)

because of the complexity of it, i also created an agent to activly builds a wiki for it [https://njlent.de/tougelike/wiki/](https://njlent.de/tougelike/wiki/) \- you can find out anything about the game and alot of its development inside there aswell. It also documents how the systems of the game were made and how they work with each other. Most of our time was spend playtesting and balacing it, but im sure there is alot that was missed. make sure to check out "how to play" in the game-menu

comments.author: SempronSixFour
comments.body: Very cool! How were the assets generated?

replies.author: noz_
replies.body: for the cars its more of a multi-step-process. at first i generated images of the style i want with nano2.1, then i gave opus those + 3d "kontext" of the general shapes of the car (either from free models or letting it manually model them from blueprint, so the shape matches). then iterating on one car to find a process that works and matches all the requirements (like tires, textures, lights etc). then reapeating that with new cars/data. All using blender mcp/scripts. The textures are then generated with codex (built in gpt-imagen) and a llittle bit of hand painting. i uploaded a few models to sketchup, to check out in detail: [https://sketchfab.com/njlent/collections/tougelike](https://sketchfab.com/njlent/collections/tougelike) \- parts of it are in the wiki aswell: [https://njlent.de/tougelike/wiki/index.html#/dev/asset-pipelines](https://njlent.de/tougelike/wiki/index.html#/dev/asset-pipelines)

comments.author: Ok_Conputa2
comments.body:
I love the look and the idea. i just played 5min so far so its  more of a first impression. The way the car always follows the road took me by suprise but i think its a neat idea, however think a bit more physics based approach would be nice with some drifting or skitting, especially when you are hit by an opponent. The boost was underwhelming, i didnt even realize that it does something, I had a car race next to me and even when boosting it had  the same speed. When the upgrades came I had no reason to care about upgrading anything. 

If it were my game I'd go all in and an exaggerated but very short boost that feels like that MIB scene. then a cooldown and quick regen, play more with physics and make it difficult to stay in control of the car. Also I'd make the menus match the resolution and style of the era you are going for. Hope that helps

replies.author: noz_
replies.body:
Thanks for the feeback! Ill try try to incorporate some of that.

For boosts its more balanced towards the endgame, when oyu have faster cars and there is alot more going on at once. There boosting also acts as a trigger for certain modules and combos, so it needs to stay sonewhat controllable.

I added stronger FX to the boost similar to the one you mentioned (toggleable in settings) which really helps to amp up the sense of speed.
